name: Guest_friendship
definition: Two individuals (or their houses), the Guest_friends, usually members of different communities, are bound by a lasting, reciprocal and often hereditary relationship that obliges each to receive, protect, feast and give gifts to the other (or his descendants) whenever he comes to the other's land. The bond is created or renewed by hospitality and by an exchange of Tokens (guest-gifts) and is held to be guaranteed by a divine Guarantor (Zeus Xenios). Unlike Guest_and_host, the relationship outlasts any single visit and is symmetrical: either party may act as host on a given occasion.

core_FEs.name: Guest_friend_1
core_FEs.definition: One party to the bond, when the parties are expressed separately.

core_FEs.name: Guest_friend_2
core_FEs.definition: The other party to the bond, when the parties are expressed separately.

core_FEs.name: Guest_friends
core_FEs.definition: Both parties expressed together (e.g. ξεῖνοι ἀλλήλων, 'guest-friends of each other').

noncore_FEs.name: Token
noncore_FEs.definition: The gift(s) exchanged to found, mark or renew the bond (ξεινήιον, arms, a bow).

noncore_FEs.name: Origin_of_bond
noncore_FEs.definition: How or when the bond arose, in particular inheritance from the parties' fathers (πατρώϊος, παλαιός).

noncore_FEs.name: Guarantor
noncore_FEs.definition: The deity held to protect guest-friends and punish violations (Ζεὺς ξείνιος).

noncore_FEs.name: Home_community
noncore_FEs.definition: The community or land of one of the parties.

noncore_FEs.name: Time
noncore_FEs.definition: When the bond was formed or exercised.

lexical_units.gloss: guest-gift as token of the bond
(of Zeus) protector of guests and guest-friends
gift that is customary (θέμις) for guests (Od. 9.268)

examples.note: Homer, Iliad 6.215, verified in the AGLDT treebank (tlg0012.tlg001); Guest_friend_2 = CNI (2sg ἐσσι, Glaukos)
Homer, Odyssey 1.187, verified in the AGLDT treebank (tlg0012.tlg002); target ξεῖνοι, reciprocal ἀλλήλων

examples.text: [τῷ|Guest_friend_2] δ' [Ὀδυσεὺς|Guest_friend_1] [ξίφος ὀξὺ καὶ ἄλκιμον ἔγχος|Token] ἔδωκεν, ἀρχὴν ξεινοσύνης προσκηδέος
examples.note: Homer, Odyssey 21.34-35, verified in the AGLDT treebank; target ξεινοσύνης; Iphitus had given Odysseus the bow

examples.text: [Ζεὺς|Guarantor] δ' ἐπιτιμήτωρ ἱκετάων τε [ξείνων|Guest_friends] τε, ξείνιος
examples.note: Homer, Odyssey 9.270-271, verified in the AGLDT treebank; target ξείνιος; here ξεῖνοι are guests in general

name: Honorific_privilege
definition: A Holder is accorded a Privilege by a Grantor (a community, a leader, an army or a god) as public recognition of the Holder's status, merit, age or role (the Basis). The Privilege may be a material share singled out for the Holder (a prize from the spoils, the choice cut of meat, an estate) or an immaterial prerogative (a seat of honour, the right to counsel, funeral rites); it both marks and constitutes the Holder's honour, so that withholding or removing it is a dishonour. The Privilege is often taken from a common Pool (spoils divided by the army, the meat of the feast).

core_FEs.name: Holder
core_FEs.definition: The person (or class, e.g. elders, the dead) to whom the Privilege belongs or is given.

core_FEs.name: Privilege
core_FEs.definition: The share or prerogative itself; often incorporated in the target (γέρας).

core_FEs.name: Grantor
core_FEs.definition: The party that accords the Privilege (δῆμος, υἷες Ἀχαιῶν, a king, a god).

core_FEs.name: Basis
core_FEs.definition: The status, merit, age or service in recognition of which the Privilege is accorded.

noncore_FEs.name: Pool
noncore_FEs.definition: The common stock from which the Privilege is taken (spoils, the feast).

noncore_FEs.name: Material_form
noncore_FEs.definition: The concrete object in which the Privilege is embodied (a tripod, a woman, the chine of an ox).

noncore_FEs.name: Manner
noncore_FEs.definition: How the Privilege is granted or held.

lexical_units.gloss: gift of honour, prize; privilege, prerogative
gift of honour (Hom. πρεσβήϊον); privilege of age
honour someone with a gift of honour

examples.text: καὶ παισὶν ἐπιτρέψειεν [ἕκαστος|Holder] κτήματ' ἐνὶ μεγάροισι γέρας θ' ὅ τι [δῆμος|Grantor] ἔδωκεν
examples.note: Homer, Odyssey 7.149-150, verified in the AGLDT treebank; target γέρας
Homer, Iliad 4.323, verified in the AGLDT treebank; Basis (age) implied by the Holder; Grantor DNI

examples.text: καὶ δή [μοι|Holder] γέρας αὐτὸς ἀφαιρήσεσθαι ἀπειλεῖς, [ᾧ ἔπι πολλὰ μόγησα|Basis], δόσαν δέ μοι [υἷες Ἀχαιῶν|Grantor]
examples.note: Homer, Iliad 1.161-162, verified in the AGLDT treebank; target γέρας

examples.text: [νώτοισιν|Material_form] δ' [Αἴαντα|Holder] [διηνεκέεσσι|Material_form] γέραιρεν [ἥρως Ἀτρεΐδης εὐρὺ κρείων Ἀγαμέμνων|Grantor]
examples.note: Homer, Iliad 7.321, verified in the AGLDT treebank; target γέραιρεν; Basis (Ajax's duel with Hector) in context

examples.text: αὐτὰρ [ἐμοὶ|Holder] γέρας αὐτίχ' ἑτοιμάσατ', ὄφρα μὴ οἶος Ἀργείων ἀγέραστος ἔω
examples.note: Homer, Iliad 1.118-119, verified in the AGLDT treebank; targets γέρας and ἀγέραστος; Grantor = CNI (2pl imperative, the Achaeans)

name: Apportioning
definition: A Distributor divides a Resource (a whole or a stock) into Shares and allots a Share to each member of a set of Recipients, according to some Basis (equality, rank, merit, the Distributor's will). Unlike Giving, which profiles a single transfer from Donor to Recipient, this frame profiles the distributive structure: one source, many recipients, each receiving his own portion, and the fairness or arbitrariness of the allotment. Typical scenes are the carving and serving of portions at a feast, the division of spoils or land, and a god's allotment of fortune to mortals.

core_FEs.name: Distributor
core_FEs.definition: The agent who divides and allots.

core_FEs.name: Recipients
core_FEs.definition: The set of individuals each of whom receives a Share; may be expressed distributively (ἑκάστῳ).

core_FEs.name: Resource
core_FEs.definition: The whole or stock that is divided (meat, wine, food, prosperity).

noncore_FEs.name: Basis
noncore_FEs.definition: The principle governing the allotment (equality, rank, merit, the Distributor's will).

noncore_FEs.name: Occasion
noncore_FEs.definition: The event at which the distribution takes place (a feast, a division of spoils).

noncore_FEs.name: Manner
noncore_FEs.definition: How the distribution is carried out.

lexical_units.gloss: dispenser, steward (of food; Zeus as dispenser of war)

examples.text: [Ζεὺς|Distributor] δ' αὐτὸς νέμει [ὄλβον|Resource] [Ὀλύμπιος|Distributor] [ἀνθρώποισιν, ἐσθλοῖς ἠδὲ κακοῖσιν|Recipients], [ὅπως ἐθέλῃσιν|Basis], [ἑκάστῳ|Recipients]
examples.note: Homer, Odyssey 6.188-189, verified in the AGLDT treebank; target νέμει

examples.text: [οἱ|Distributor] δ' ἤδη [μοίρας|Shares] τ' ἔνεμον κερόωντό τε οἶνον
examples.note: Homer, Odyssey 8.470, verified in the AGLDT treebank; target ἔνεμον; Recipients DNI (the banqueters)

examples.text: καὶ ταμίαι παρὰ νηυσὶν ἔσαν [σίτοιο|Resource] δοτῆρες
examples.note: Homer, Iliad 19.44, verified in the AGLDT treebank; target δοτῆρες (incorporates the Distributor); Recipients DNI (the army)
